attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. He presents the scenario as his position.

semantics.note: The 80% loss is tied to his stated scenario that the vast majority of data centers go unused, and the drafter keeps that as the antecedent. 'Will be lost' is firm wording, and the threshold and causal clause are kept.

contract.note: Reading loss as principal not recovered after recoveries is the ordinary reading of 'funds lost'. The contract correctly requires the non-use condition to be shown first.

evidence.note: CBRE H1 2026 report, published 2026-08-27, before the evaluation date. Low leasing vacancy in North America argues against widespread empty facilities, but it does not measure compute use or debt losses, so it cannot show the antecedent or the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. Nothing in the packet shows that the vast majority of AI data centers went unused, so the antecedent's status is unknown. No sector-wide loss data exist either. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The demand antecedent, 'vast majority' and 'will collapse' are all kept. The parenthetical claim about profitability is rightly left out of this claim.

contract.note: The speaker did not define the scale of the demand shortfall, the set of projects counted, or what 'collapse' means. The contract's readings (insolvency, default or financial closure; an overwhelming majority) are ordinary ones, and it says plainly that the antecedent is unknown.

evidence.note: Sightline report of Feb 2026 on the 190GW pipeline he cited. It measures announced capacity, not paying demand, so it neither shows nor rules out the antecedent.
Secondary compilation dated 2026-10-17 reporting no public neocloud GPU-loan defaults. It is not a complete census and cannot settle an open-ended conditional forecast.

reviews.rationale: The demand-shortfall antecedent has not been established, and no deadline was stated. A conditional with an unknown antecedent is not scored. The few defaults on record neither support nor contradict the forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion, which he stresses is not hyperbole.

semantics.note: A present-tense claim about who compute revenue depends on, with 'vast majority' kept. Calling the two companies unsustainable is a characterisation built into the claim.

contract.note: The Q1 2026 period, the sector boundary and the test for dependence are evaluator choices, but reasonable ones. Using his own 70–90% figure to anchor 'vast majority' is fair to him.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of a $30B round in Feb 2026. It shows financing at the scale he mentions, but nothing about compute-provider revenue share or a need to raise that much every year.
OpenAI's own announcement of $110B in new investment in Feb 2026. It is financing, not realized compute revenue, and does not show an annual funding need.

reviews.rationale: Both items are company disclosures confirming large fundraising. Neither gives a sector-wide compute-revenue total, a share attributable to OpenAI and Anthropic, or cash-flow evidence of an annual financing need. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I think we'll see' states belief, not graded probability, and the second sentence is a plain 'will'. I treat this as a scored forecast with no deadline. The perception-management motive is part of the claim.

contract.note: Requiring multiple rescue deals plus evidence of the stated motive follows his own words. The contract correctly says isolated cancellations cannot falsify a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: News report of 2026-10-19 that Microsoft withdrew from one delayed Nscale site because of power supply. It tempers the 'anywhere they see it' wording but cannot disprove a forecast of a few future rescues, and it is not itself a rescue.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the packet shows no qualifying rescue deals with evidence of the motive. Microsoft's withdrawal from a single site is not a conclusive contrary event. Absence of rescues so far is not failure, so the forecast stays open.
